posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
Generally speaking:
Most of the complaints about the forums come from people who neither read the rules, nor comprehend why they exist.  Then, they exaggerate things that happened.
Just as an example from the thread
"I hate the rules on Necroposting!" and then comment on plugins... which don't have a Necroposting rule apply, just because of what they are.
Rules - FORUM RULES
Welcome to the official RPG Maker forums. We have a short list of simple to follow rules, so please read through them below. Individual subforums may have more specific rules or exceptions to these rules.  NOTE: This is the official forum for RPG Maker products and Visual Novel Maker. We do not...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
That's not to say there aren't bad actors.  There absolutely are.  But, every forum has them.
I touched on some of the bad behaviors in this thread:
Has anything weird or bad happened here recently?
If it's any consolation, everyone, Turan and I have a DM thread where we often have a good laugh at the people who are consistently misinterpreting neutral advice as personal attacks.  Also what's wrong is that I haven't been around much lately. I have a natural aura that calms everyone down, so...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
However, you'll find that most often on these forums, you get someone new who comes in out of "bad faith" and is just generally very intent on being a "bad actor", then wondering why they get the pushback they do.
Things like, "I'm going to introduce myself by telling everyone my every single character flaw" generally don't go over well in any community (and we do have a fair share of people who engage in that) or "why is nobody helping me?!" followed by some of the most inflammatory and incendiary things a person can say without jumping to expletives.
Is there a grain of truth in nearly every complaint about the forums?  Yeah, most of them, from what I've read.
But, are they highly exaggerated?  Usually.
Were they in the wrong?  If you manage to track down their original posts, yeah, usually.  They are usually lashing out irrationally at things like advice (because we don't tend to sugarcoat anything here).
Do you sometimes find a bad actor who the person was "feeding the troll" with?  Yeah, sometimes.
Some of it is a matter of perspective.  Those looking to be victims always find a way to portray themselves as such.  Those looking to make friendships and learn, will find that, too.
EDIT:  I should probably also point out that people who complain about the forums on Reddit will rarely give exactly what they asked, or the username they signed up with.  I usually take that as "an admission of guilt".  Why?  Trying to hide their interactions in the forum is a good way to avoid responsibility if you were actually at fault.

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
Tai is really accomodating today, writing a WoT that can be read in under 10 minutes ;D
A lot of the people on the forums who have the actual skills to help (as you need a deeper understanding of how the program work and even more detail knowledge when it comes to special topics like resources or actual code writing) have been around for many many years.
For me, this has of course left it's traces. My experience is mainly resource related, cause that is where I usually dwell.
I have seen how many people out of the ones starting finish their games... not so many. And generally speaking, those who get anything done are those with a certain amount of patience and will to learn. This extends to reading the rules, trying to improve their own skill within reason and so on.
I have set up some rules for myself to save myself from frustration when I even take the time answering a resource request, though there might be the odd one out where I do it anyways or try to explain someone why they don't get help.
a) is when people ask for help, but are so impatient or thoughtless that they leave half the information out, which makes it impossible to help them without sinking quite some time upfront, pulling the infromation from them.
b) is when people ask for free custom resources (aka things I cannot just post for everyone to use in the end, like edits of paid tiles or custom characters or styles that don't mesh) when the game is not finished yet and it's just a placeholder to swap. I have made a lot of resources in my early days that are just on my hard drive. Custom sprites of special characters and poses for games very long dead. Time wasted if not for the practise. I really don't wanna know how real that is for all the plugin help requests, how many lines of code have been written for games that are dead by now or just features that were scrapped later on...
c) is when people ask for too unreasonably much. Yeah, I can make resources and I know from exchange with other artists that I am a pretty speedy one - and still every now and then someone pops up and wants something done that would take me more than a workday to do. Sure this is my hobby in a way, but not like that.
d) is when they simply come off as unlikeable. Call me a diva, but if I already see in their post history that they don't answer nicely to responses, don't bother to say thanks after someone helped them out and get nasty when explained that something doesn't work as planned, why exactly should I be inclined to help them? I always wonder if they are like that in real life. Like... if some stranger kindly asks me if I can spend a few minutes helping them out with something (safely in public, lol), I do that, if they rudely demand it, then I don't. Carefully writing a complete post like talking to a real human you take serious while trying to not twist the grammar and spelling too much goes a very long way.
Maybe I missed something, but there are plenty of resource requests that go unanswered even if I could, just cause I don't want my mood to be pulled down by pouring energy and time and always a bit of heartblood into people that just suck it up.
Those things happen across all boards in various forms, and I bet that is the people who then complain that someone told them why they are not getting the help they want or didn't get the help they want.
Other people are different, of course, but in general, I have not really seen someone being flamed for just being inexperienced. We have mods here and we have plenty of people who started out in the forums pretty much at 0 and got along well.
Alone in this year, I have probably solved or helped with nearly a triple digit amount of resource requests (maybe I should count it out one day, upper double digits for sure), and still we lately had a lovely person writing an inflammatory post how people in resource requests don't ever get help (among other similarly true and selfaware things).
To be fair: I don't mind if that type of people don't stay and go back to reddit or whatever.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
I thought about creating a tutorial with an example place, called Tutorial Town, as described in the
help file
. It was going to have an example of how to do everything in RPG Maker. Introduce some basic scripting such as one example per call from
the API documentation
. It would take quite a while. It would be comparable to the few RPG Maker books I've taken a look through. It might not be as good as the
old tutorials though
. They were great resources for starting. When upgraded to MZ, these resources would have helped me a lot.
In the Japanese forums, they use a system of question/solved next to the post name. Sometimes the mods might add tags to it, but not always. There should be a knowledge engine or something. For people under 18, and some over 18, learning to program can be difficult. Asking for help can be equally as difficult. When I was learning programming concepts at 12, my friend and I had a hard time starting. We made a lot of mistakes, but we also didn't have the internet or references. We just had a help file, determination, and laughs. Picking up something like RPG Maker could be daunting and any kind of criticism can be discouraging.
Sometimes I think about the forum rules on necro-posting like old StackOverflow memes about years old unanswered questions.
Sometimes I never see a post until years later while looking for something else. I have the answer, but I remember necro-posting and sigh. In contrast, the rule is good for IT conventions in archiving.
Overall, these threads leave me with a lot of questions:
What would make the forums better?
What makes good members?
How to have a good introduction to this forum's etiquette?
How to invite new developers and users to events and learning?
How to have quality curation without elitism?
How can people from different backgrounds respect and admire another?

posts.author: Popoto_milk
posts.body:
I don't think the RPG Maker forums are perfect when it comes to dealing with newbies and such. I do think there are times where there's too much hostility or unhelpful answers. But some people seem to forget they're not talking to their internet company's customer support. Far more often, it's the users rather than the forum that's the problem.
If you don't want to put in basic effort then you deserve to get filtered.
Something like "read this" or especially "do the tutorial" are minor, bare minimum things. If you don't want to do those things, you don't deserve help. Google searching is also something you should be doing but at least there you have to put in sometimes large amounts of effort.
Aside from that, how you ask questions is on you. It sounds like the reddit OP didn't know how to ask(if you already did the tutorial twice, why didn't you point it out in the thread?). To be honest, I've seen this type of attitude before and it's infuriating. These guys will really play up their point of view, but if you ever get to see any actual proof of their assertions, it's an entirely different story. I wouldn't be surprised if "I did the tutorial twice" really means "I did it until I got bored halfway through" or "I did it while watching TV"

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Actually these types of threads often turn up on Reddit. You'd likely find similar posts with a google search.
As mentioned by Tai, typically the poster on reddit is exaggerating things quite a lot.
They also tend to base their whole experience on one interaction, often citing Andar or Turan as trouble makers.
Andar is Andar, I won't say anything more.
Turan is pretty matter-of-fact about his posts, I'd say neither inflammatory nor supportive, and as such some people tend to either misunderstand his passive voice or just don't find it agreeable.
Maybe some of the other regulars who often assist, including myself, may be perceived in a similar way in the manner in which they voice their help.
Regardless, I find the people who flock to the RM Reddit as people I would not want to interact with and likely just make my RMW ignore list twice as long, if not thrice. There was a particular thread I had read where, although made as a joke, spoke volumes to me how they perceive their "victim-hood" in getting assistance here. They joked about "needing a therapy session" after using RMW.
As Popoto mentioned with doing tutorials and googling; when it comes to game development, likely one of the most important skills is self-reliance; the ability to act on seeking knowledge and gaining knowledge.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
It’s kind of become an ongoing meme among my circle. Basically, anyone who can’t express themselves properly, refuses to put in even the slightest bit of effort, or acts like an entitled brat ends up making a thread here, fails to behave decently, and then runs off to cry about how “awful” the forum is for not babysitting them.
Honestly, every piece of information you could ever need about making something in RPG Maker has already been shared a thousand times over. Yet the genuinely helpful folks here still take the time to explain things again and again to newcomers. And not just newcomers, either. I’ve been on the receiving end of plenty of helpful people myself and still am.
In my opinion, the problem isn’t the forum. The problem is people who haven’t matured, even well into their 30s. Being told to do a tutorial, watch a video, or learn the basics is the bare minimum effort anyone should be willing to put in. But some take it as an insult and throw a tantrum on Reddit, where plenty of like-minded man-children are ready to back them up.

I don't think that's necessary and would be so massive that it becomes cumbersome to use. You just gotta be using search engines smartly. If you really happen to have something so complex that it has been never conceived before, don't just google How to do X with Y". You gotta be more specific on the issue.
And then, if that doesn't work, go ahead and make a thread, using the great template. Show people that you've done your homework, but can't seem to solve it by yourself. Be kind, be thankful. Of course people are going to recommend a different approach from yours if they think theirs is easier or more efficient. Those people are not giving "useless advice" as so many of these people claim.
Even someone in OPs posted reddit post acknowledged that the reddit sub is good for "obvious questions", which is what we here *apparently* attack people for (never seen it tho). And that the forum is way better for more complex issues.
Overall I think my point stands about people's behavior, and this is a little bit of a derailing imho, so I'm just gonna leave it at that.

posts.body:
People who use RPG maker are not ing professional game devs we're using it cause we want to make something quick.
Click to expand...
This line tells you everything you need to know about the OP. Seems to me like they aren't patient enough to do anything that requires effort and just want quick results. And if you don't want to put in effort yourself, why should others put in effort to help you?
I won't deny the forum does kinda suck sometimes, just like pretty much every other large community, reddit included. But I've yet to see a situation where people get "irrationally angry" over someone asking a question. More often than not, the anger is justified, for one of several reasons:
Other members ask follow up questions, because there's not enough context to help. Then the person in question gets defensive and offended that people are questioning them.
The exact same question had been asked and answered multiple times.
The question was posted in the wrong section (e.g. asking how to install and use resources, in a free resource thread that specifically says not to do so)
Asking for help with AI generated stuff. Chances are, anyone proficient enough in their craft would not want to help fix AI slop.
The person in question is rude, entitled, or otherwise unpleasant to deal with.
With people like these, even if I could easily help, for the sake of my own sanity, I would not. These kind of people are just one of the reasons I say the forum kinda sucks sometimes.
